diagram_math_checks.objects: The two-dimensional B-space and its twelve roots, with Euclidean embedding E(x a_s+y a_t)=(x-3y/2,sqrt(3)y/2).
diagram_math_checks.check: Dot products give Gram matrix [[1,-3/2],[-3/2,3]], exactly step 2.1 and F2/F4. Thus E is a B-isometry, not an orthonormal plot of coefficient pairs; the simple angle is 150 degrees.

Step 2.2 pairs (1,0),(3,1),(2,1),(3,2),(1,1),(0,1) embed at angles 0,30,60,90,120,150 degrees; their negatives supply 180 through 330. Squared norms are respectively 1,3,1,3,1,3. Exact Fraction calculations checked all 12 vectors, the norm formula, positive determinants of successive ordered vectors and squared cosine 3/4 for each adjacent pair. Source decimal 1.732050808 is the drawing approximation to sqrt(3), with exact lengths stated in prose.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Simple root reflections V to V.
diagram_math_checks.check: F14 with the Gram matrix yields r_s(x,y)=(-x+3y,y) and r_t(x,y)=(x,x-y), as in step 2.2; the reflection axes are perpendicular to the arrows. Exact calculations checked preservation of all twelve coefficient pairs under both maps, the Cartan matrix [[2,-1],[-3,2]], and integrality of all 144 root-coroot pairings.

F4 and step 5.1 map each beta to (sqrt(3)/2)beta^vee = sqrt(3) beta/B(beta,beta). This keeps every directed ray, sends squared length 1 to 3 and 3 to 1, and sends a_s to a_s prime and a_t to a_t prime on the 0 and 150 degree rays. Off-diagonal pairings become -3 and -1, so its Cartan matrix is A transpose, matching step 2.1. The picture exchanges red/blue on all twelve rays.

No diagram is used by Verification or Facts. All original bytes remain a prefix of the current carrier; the figure only illustrates steps 2.1, 2.2 and 5.1. No statements, hypotheses, dependencies, sources or status changed.
